retrievalContext:
Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Every person in need, regardless of background and papers, is welcome at the Humanitarian Service Point in the Amsterdam office of The Netherlands Red Cross.

For everyone who visits, the situation is examined and a possible solution is sought.

To find a solution, the Red Cross is also dependent on available assistance from other organizations.

Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Here, representatives of The Netherlands Red Cross are present to listen and give advice to visitors.

You can also use their WiFi, chargers, toilets and get something to drink.

If you need to, you can also rest here.

Unfortunately, they do not provide shelter.

That is a municipal task.

Document: How can I get support with clothes?  

The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  

https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/  For most recent information on initiatives that provide support in clothes or offer clothes for a small price see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace

Document: How to file a complaint about a shelter from the Red Cross?

If the shelter is run by the Red Cross, you can fill in a complaint here: https://www.rodekruis.nl/en/contact/complaints-or-suggestions/

Document: Can the Dutch Red Cross provide medical assistance?  

We can provide you with general information about healthcare and medical assistance in the Netherlands.

However, it is important to note that the Dutch Red Cross does not offer direct medical assistance.   

It might be confusing, as other national Red Cross societies may offer medical assistance in their countries, but the Dutch Red Cross does not provide this.

Document: Red Cross The Red Cross focuses on humanitarian assistance, they offer for example; first aid, emergency food support and psychosocial support.  

Through the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp (https://wa.me/31614458781]) they can connect you to available help.

Document: Can the Red Cross provide me with a place to live?

The Red Cross is not responsible for the placement of people in the shelters.

This is done by the municipality.

The Red Cross does help in the management of some shelters, but most shelters are run by municipalities and other organizations.

This means that the Red Cross cannot influence the placement in shelters.

You should go to one of the registration points to get shelter.   

For more information, please see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/109-shelter

Document: Can I switch from one shelter to another location?                                                                                                                                                                                                           

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.

Document: How can I get food support?  

When you are staying in a public shelter, please approach someone from the shelter to ask where you can find additional food support.

You can also contact the Red Cross Food Program Helpdesk.

For all general questions, new applications, extension requests, etc, PA's can call/text/

WhatsApp them at +31 97010259797 (Mon-Fri 9:00 – 17:00).  

In municipalities all over the country Voedselbank Nederland (Food Bank Netherlands) distributes food parcels to displaced persons from Ukraine.

Too find out if you are eligible, please see: https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/

Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?  

Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

Document: Can the Red Cross mediate between me and the hospital or make medical requests on my behalf?

You may receive requests to mediate with hospitals or make medical requests on someone’s behalf.

The Netherlands Red Cross does not handle such requests.

Below is a template to respond.  

Template for medical requests  Thank you for your message.

The Dutch Red Cross does not process medical requests, either within the Netherlands or internationally.

You must contact the clinic in their destination country or in the Netherlands directly.

However, it is possible that the doctor you contacted in your country can help you to contact the doctor in the country where you are planning to move.   

There are two options:  1.

The doctor in your hospital can contact the doctor in the country where you seek treatment.

2.

A doctor in your country can write a medical report that you can take with you.

However, this does not guarantee fast or identical treatment, as medical procedures vary per country.

In the Netherlands, patients must first register with a general practitioner (GP), who will review the medical report.  

I hope that this information helps!

Feel free to reach out to us with further questions.

Document: Remaining Undocumented If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status you will become *undocumented*.

Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies.

However, you still have the right to necesarry medical care, judicial assistance and children under 18 have to right to attend school as well.  

You can choose to apply for asylum at any point with undocumented status.  

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Document: What to do (as a receptionist/aid worker) when a displaced person from Ukraine reports at an NLRC office?

It might happen that someone therefore is going to an office of the Red Cross to ask for help.

Step 1: try to find out:  - If the person has Ukrainian nationality or a permanent residence permit for Ukraine?

Document: Requesting shelter upon arrival in the NL as required by Dutch law.

*Cited directly from the Dutch government website*:  It is very difficult at the moment for local authorities to arrange accomodation.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

This applies to both refugees who have been in the Netherlands for some time and new arrivals.

If not possible to find a place of residence, please report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.  

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.   

[*Dutch Government website*](https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay)

- If you are currently in private shelter and looking for alternatives, please consult the municipality where you are staying for further guidance.

- Apart from Municipal and Private Accommodation, you can also explore finding independent housing, such as rentals, purchases, boarding houses, hostels, etc. -

If you are currently in Ukraine or another country and planning to come to the Netherlands, you can find information here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/126-arrival-in-the-netherlands   Need help for shelter of housing in the Netherlands?

Visit http://www.refugeehelp.nl for comprehensive information on available options for shelter and housing in the Netherlands.

Document: Can I get shelter in the Netherlands if I am already registered in another Schengen country?

Yes, if you are registered in a Schengen country but you want to come to the Netherlands and apply for shelter here, please make sure you have the Ukrainian nationality or permanent residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26th November, 2021.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

Document: Can I stay in the shelter with my pet?  

Yes, you can.

However, please note that centers are overcrowded, and space for pets is very limited.

Availability depends on the municipality.

Therefore it is very possible that there is no place for you and the pet together.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100049-pets

Document: Netherlands (but not Amsterdam/Utrecht/Swolgen/Heerevenveen/Rotterdam/Haarlem) General advise If you’re coming to the Netherlands with a Ukrainian passport/valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit and proof you left Ukraine after November 26, 2021, you have a right to Shelter & Temporary Protection.

To apply, visit the municipality office in the city where you will arrive.  

Please note that the housing situation here is challenging and becoming more restricted.

We recommend contacting us before you leave to get the latest updates.  

If possible, try to arrange accommodation on your own when arriving in the Netherlands.

Note that you need a local address (accommodation) to apply for temporary protection.   

Actions to take when general advise was not sufficient NO referrals for cases outside of the Netherlands.

Advise the PA to contact us upon arrival.   

Actions to take when general advise is not sufficient If the PA shares challenges in finding a place to stay, please consult with the Team Captain.

Document: What should I do if I return to the Netherlands after a period in Ukraine (or another country)?

What to do on return: - When you return to the Netherlands, you must report again to the municipality or municipal reception center where you previously stayed.

- If you have lost your shelter place as a result of the earlier (temporary) departure and the living allowance has been stopped, it will be assessed whether you comply with the applicable rules at the time of your return.

If this is the case, you are again entitled to childcare and the other benefits in kind from the ROOO.

- If you have been deregistered from the BRP, registration must be done again.   

What to do with earlier advice on a shelter location in case of temporary departure: - At the moment, municipalities are advised to maintain a shelter for displaced persons who leave the municipal shelter for less than 14 days.

- This advice was issued mid-2022 and remains valid.

In case of a departure of more than 14 days, the municipality can give the reception place to someone else, for example if the occupancy rate is high.

Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Every person in need, regardless of background and papers, is welcome at the Humanitarian Service Point in the Amsterdam office of The Netherlands Red Cross.

For everyone who visits, the situation is examined and a possible solution is sought.

To find a solution, the Red Cross is also dependent on available assistance from other organizations.

Document: Amsterdam (e-mail !)

HSP is closed Ukrainians in Amsterdam can report to the municipality directly via opvangoekraine@amsterdam.nl   

Sometimes, the person may initially receive a rejection due to the current situation in NL.

We recommend following up on the response and continuing communication with the municipality via the same email.

In your follow-up, kindly explain your situation, where you're staying, and how long you can stay there.

Also, include any important details about your circumstances, such as medical conditions, young children, or other special needs

Document: Can I switch from one shelter to another location?                                                                                                                                                                                                           

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.

Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Here, representatives of The Netherlands Red Cross are present to listen and give advice to visitors.

You can also use their WiFi, chargers, toilets and get something to drink.

If you need to, you can also rest here.

Unfortunately, they do not provide shelter.

That is a municipal task.

Document: What do I say when someone offers to host a displaced person from Ukraine?  

We created a standard template for a reply to people who offer to host a displaced person from Ukraine:   

Dear [Name],  Thank you to those who have offered their support.

(adjust to the question)  

The national organization RefugeeHomeNL (Private Shelter for Ukrainian Displaced Persons), of which the Dutch Red Cross was a part, ended late 2023.

This means that we are currently unable to match host households with Ukrainian displaced persons.  

If you would like to open your home to Ukrainian displaced persons, we recommend that you inform your local municipality.

This includes the people working at the reception desk, if for example the shelter is a hotel.

The people on the ground are better equipped to handle the complaint, as they can forward it to the municipality.  

If the person has discussed it with the location manager, but does not feel helped, they can file a complaint with the municipality.

Check on the website of the municipality how to make a complaint.  

Please note, for internal use only: if both the municipality and the shelter are not assisting and you feel like the case is urgent, please report it to your Team Captain.

He/she can take over the case and if necessary report it to our local colleagues in the district.

Always check whether the location is run by the Red Cross or not!

Document: Red Cross The Red Cross focuses on humanitarian assistance, they offer for example; first aid, emergency food support and psychosocial support.  

Through the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp (https://wa.me/31614458781]) they can connect you to available help.

Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Every person in need, regardless of background and papers, is welcome at the Humanitarian Service Point in the Amsterdam office of The Netherlands Red Cross.

For everyone who visits, the situation is examined and a possible solution is sought.

To find a solution, the Red Cross is also dependent on available assistance from other organizations.

Document: Can the Dutch Red Cross provide medical assistance?  

We can provide you with general information about healthcare and medical assistance in the Netherlands.

However, it is important to note that the Dutch Red Cross does not offer direct medical assistance.   

It might be confusing, as other national Red Cross societies may offer medical assistance in their countries, but the Dutch Red Cross does not provide this.

Document: Netherlands Red Cross Amsterdam Here, representatives of The Netherlands Red Cross are present to listen and give advice to visitors.

You can also use their WiFi, chargers, toilets and get something to drink.

If you need to, you can also rest here.

Unfortunately, they do not provide shelter.

That is a municipal task.

Document: Food support per city The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of food options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Document: Huisartsenpost Amsterdam When you are in Amsterdam you can call or visit this place if you feel very sick outside of times that regular health services are open.  

+31 88 - 00 30 600 (17:00 - 08:00)  https://www.huisartsenpostenamsterdam.nl/  

If it's life-threatening: Call 112 instead!

Document: What are the roles and responsibilities of aid organizations?

The two main aid organizations that can help you are the Red Cross and Vluchtelingenwerk

Document: Can the Red Cross mediate between me and the hospital or make medical requests on my behalf?

You may receive requests to mediate with hospitals or make medical requests on someone’s behalf.

The Netherlands Red Cross does not handle such requests.

Below is a template to respond.  

Template for medical requests  Thank you for your message.

The Dutch Red Cross does not process medical requests, either within the Netherlands or internationally.

You must contact the clinic in their destination country or in the Netherlands directly.

However, it is possible that the doctor you contacted in your country can help you to contact the doctor in the country where you are planning to move.   

There are two options:  1.

The doctor in your hospital can contact the doctor in the country where you seek treatment.

2.

A doctor in your country can write a medical report that you can take with you.

However, this does not guarantee fast or identical treatment, as medical procedures vary per country.

In the Netherlands, patients must first register with a general practitioner (GP), who will review the medical report.  

I hope that this information helps!

Feel free to reach out to us with further questions.

Document: Helpdesk Red Cross If you have questions regarding food, shelter, medical help, your situation or any other help you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp

[here](https://wa.me/31614458781)  General helpdesk from the Red Cross, we can help to connect you with the right help available.

Document: Can I switch from one shelter to another location?                                                                                                                                                                                                           

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.

Document: Can the Red Cross provide me with a place to live?

The Red Cross is not responsible for the placement of people in the shelters.

This is done by the municipality.

The Red Cross does help in the management of some shelters, but most shelters are run by municipalities and other organizations.

This means that the Red Cross cannot influence the placement in shelters.

You should go to one of the registration points to get shelter.

Document: What facilities should be available at a Crisis Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -

Document: What is the stance of the Red Cross when somebody is not helped at HSP?  

We do our best to ensure that people arriving at an Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) are directed to the most appropriate form of assistance for them.

This could mean that people are directed to Ter Apel, rather than assistance being provided at the HSP.

However, we try to ensure that all refugees have their basic needs met, i.e. they can have some food and a drink, rest and charge mobile devices before travelling onwards.

Document: What does a Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) offer?

Humanitarian Service Points are run by the Red Cross.

At a Humanitarian Service Point you can rest, eat and drink something, and charge your phone.

You will receive further information about how shelter is arranged in the Netherlands, and the journey onward.

Humanitarian Service Points are not registration locations.

They are intended as a place where you can rest and to help you on your way.

At a registration location, the municipality determines who does and does not have access to shelter and you are registered.

At Humanitarian Service Points, Red Cross employees inform you about the options for shelter, but they do not determine any policies.

Document: Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.

The Red Cross cannot arrange shelter independently.

This must go through the municipality, RCVS, or LCVS.

Requests can be send to humanitairehelpdesk.westnederland@rodekruis.nl.

These requests will be handled on Thursday but urgent requests can be picked up sooner.

They are also reachable through phone/WhatsApp at +31618270562.  

Address  Zilverstraat 2 2544ER Den Haag
